content.text:
Image 1: Four-panel storyboard reference, used for the overall shot structure, shot sizes, and camera-movement rhythm. Read it from left to right and from top to bottom; panel N is Shot N. It is a line-art sketch: do not adopt its sketch style, black outlines, white background, panel borders or drawn faces.
Image 2: Reference of INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, a rendered set, not live action. Use it only for the room's layout, the furniture's positions and the light's direction; do not reference its visual content. It contains no people.
Image 3: Reference of INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 4: Reference of INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 5: Reference of INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 6: Reference of INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 7: Blocking reference of the segment's start: the same place with these people in their places, used only for where each person is and which way they face; take faces and outfits from each subject's own image. It is a line-art diagram: do not adopt its outlines or white background.
Image 8: Subject 1 (Ji Ran, look S0) character appearance reference.
Image 9: Prop 1 (pour-over coffee equipment) maps to this image; copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 9.
From each prop's image, use only structure, material, and color.
[Subject settings]
Subject 1 (Ji Ran): Refer to Image 8. 27, heroine; owner of Jiejian Company, an architecture and interior design firm; daughter of Ji Hongyuan. Outfit: look S0: Office, day one: a fitted dove-grey silk button-down shirt with long sleeves, tucked in, the top two buttons open. A black high-waisted bodycon pencil skirt to just above the knee, cinched at the waist with a thin black leather belt. Black pointed-toe stiletto pumps. Signature colour: black.
Environment (INT. JI RAN'S OFFICE): Refer to Images 2 to 6. Day, soft daylight through the floor-to-ceiling windows. Soft daylight from the windows behind the desk, warm recessed ceiling spots and the black task lamp on the desk. Quiet office hum and the trickle of coffee.
Do not swap the characters' appearances, clothing, actions, positions or dialogue.
[Subjects and relationships]
Only one person appears throughout: Ji Ran.
[Blocking]
Refer to Images 2 to 6 for the room and Image 7 for the people's places. Ji Ran stands behind the walnut executive desk, which is centred in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows. She faces the front pin-up wall, with the high-backed black leather chair behind her. She wears the fitted dove-grey silk shirt and the black bodycon pencil skirt. She holds the black gooseneck kettle over the glass V60 dripper, which sits on its glass server at the pour-over station on the desk. The white coffee cup sits on its saucer beside the station. The desktop also holds spread architectural plans, a fan of wood samples and the small brushed-metal figurine. Camera side: in front of the desk, on the pin-up wall side, facing the desk and the windows.
[Overall style]
Photorealistic live-action short drama with cinematic lighting. Each character keeps the face and the outfit with its main colour from their reference image throughout. Use each character sheet only for that character: the face from the close-up on the right, the body and outfit from the turnaround on the left; do not render the sheet's layout, white background or multiple views. This segment has 2 lines, in this order: Su Yaqing (V.O.), Ji Ran. Generate speech only from the lines in {} in the shot list, each spoken exactly once by its speaker; everyone else keeps their mouth naturally closed while listening, and a V.O. speaker keeps their mouth closed or is off screen. Follow the shot list below; do not add cuts or camera moves beyond it. Strictly adhere to the 180-degree rule: within a scene, characters keep their screen sides and the camera stays on one side of the axis. Seamless continuity of action; cut on action. For dialogue prefer static shot-reverse-shot and over-the-shoulder shots, balanced with reaction shots and close-up inserts. Faces stable and clear, with no resemblance to any real actor or actress. Normal human eyes. Natural anatomy. Natural, fluid motion that follows the blocking; characters make subtle, natural movements. Characters, props and environment share one world with matched lighting. Each line ends naturally with breathing room and is never cut off. Authentic performances with micro-expressions. No BGM; generate only dialogue, environmental sounds and action sounds. No subtitles.
[Continuity]
Maintain continuity in the identities, number, appearance, clothing, relative heights, spatial positions, and eyelines of all the characters. The actions in the shot list occur strictly in sequence. Hands are anatomically correct.
[Strictly exclude]
subtitles or garbled text. malformed hands on the kettle. added characters. Dialogue from the wrong character, multiple people speaking at once, repeated or missing lines, lip-sync errors and audio-visual desynchronization. The raw reference images (character sheets, setting plates) appearing as a frame of the video, and starting on a still frame of the setting reference. A fast zoom-in at the start, a fast pull-back at the end, unmotivated whip-pans, tilts, zooms and 360-degree orbits. Axis-crossing, jump cuts, frame skips, flicker and clipping. Face swaps, changes in age or clothing, sudden height shifts, added or missing characters, spatial jumps, and disordered action sequences; props popping in or vanishing, and duplicate characters except mirror reflections. Hand clipping, extra fingers, fused fingers, malformed hands. Subtitles, captions, watermarks and garbled writing; writing and logos other than those on a key prop's reference image, which are copied from it; a phone screen or paper that is not a key prop is shown from the back or out of focus. Black-and-white, monochrome, grayscale, desaturated visuals; hand-drawn, sketch, line art, illustration, comics, animation; storyboard frames, rough sketches, panel borders, gutters and grid layouts.
[Shot list] (4 shots, approximately 10 seconds)
When a previous-shot reference image is given, it is the moment this segment starts from: keep its people's positions, outfits, props and light, and continue from there. Shot 1 keeps its own camera, matching the image's framing only when it frames the same view; do not repeat that frame later.
Shot 1 (0-3s): [Wide shot, fast push in, eye level, from the pin-up wall facing the desk and the windows] The sleek office with the city skyline behind the glass. Ji Ran stands behind the walnut desk among the plans and wood samples, pouring a thin stream from the black kettle into the dripper. Her lips stay closed. Dialogue (Su Yaqing, V.O., in Chinese, teasing and sing-song): {听说你爸想让你跟路少泽联姻，} <Water trickles through the paper filter>
Shot 2 (3-5s): [Close-up insert, locked-off camera, high angle, from the front of the desk looking down at the pour-over station] Ji Ran's hand circles the gooseneck kettle, and the water spirals over the coffee grounds in the glass dripper. Dialogue (Su Yaqing, V.O., in Chinese, gossipy): {你当年那么爱他，}
Shot 3 (5-7s): [Medium shot, locked-off camera, eye level, from the front of the desk] Ji Ran sets the kettle down and braces one hand flat on the desk beside the plans. Her mouth stays closed and her expression turns cold. Dialogue (Su Yaqing, V.O., in Chinese, drawn out and mocking): {怎么样是不是很开心啊？}
Shot 4 (7-10s): [Medium close-up, slight push in, low angle, from the front of the desk] Ji Ran lifts her eyes toward the pin-up wall with a flat, icy half-smile, her hand still braced on the desk. Dialogue (Ji Ran, in Chinese, deadpan and cold): {开心，他死了我更开心。}
At the end: Ji Ran stands behind the walnut executive desk in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows. One hand is braced on the desktop, and she faces the pin-up wall with a cold expression. The kettle rests beside the dripper and server at the pour-over station, and the white cup is on its saucer.

Image 10 is the first frame.
